newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mixed in Calif. nuke watch.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mixed in Calif. nuke watch.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mixed Friday as traders waited for two California nuclear units to return to full electrical output, industry sources said.
"No one wants to short this market until those (San Onofre) units are fully back," said one Western electricity trader.

The 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre (SONGS) unit 3 remained off line with a restart expected Sunday night while engineers corrected a water contamination problem in the unit's lube oil system, the operator said.
The unit, in San Clemente, Calif., was earlier scheduled to return to service yesterday.
The adjacent 1,070 MW unit 2 was holding at 70 percent power while maintenance work on a main feedwater pump was being carried out.
August Palo Verde (PV) futures fell initially Friday morning in line with lower physical prices in the U.S. West, the sources said, but values later climbed.

As of 1220 EDT, August PV was trading up 12 cents at $36.80 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges at $36.40-37.00, while September was bid at $29.05 and offered at $29.20 following trade at $28.90 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) was up 11 cents at $22.15 per MWh after exchanges in a range of $21.90-22.15, while September was trading up two cents at the day's high of $22.15 after a low of $21.95 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1145 EDT an estimated total of 51 COB and 200 PV contracts had traded.
In generation news, output at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Richland, Washington, rose to 92 percent of capacity as of early Friday.
The 750 MW Mohave coal-fired unit 3, which was shut Monday for repairs, was expected to resume operations Saturday.
The 254 MW Valmy coal-fired unit 1 in Nevada was unlikely to return to full power until the weekend, after its output was halved Tuesday because of a tube leak.
Separately, southbound capacity on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie transmission system was set to be cut by 250 MW to 3,200 MW today between 0900 and 1600 PDT for maintenance work.
